from manim import *
import numpy as np

# Use the provided TeachingScene base class without modification.
class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "Prerequisite: The Matrix as a Machine"
        lecture_lines = [
            "A 2x2 matrix acts like a function on space.",
            "It transforms every point in the 2D grid.",
            "We represent this transformation as T(v) = Av."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_MATRIX = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_FORMULA = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_CAT = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_MATRIX)
        
        # 2D Grid (NumberPlane)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4.0,
            y_length=4.0,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False} 
        )
        # Place in the area from B2 to F6
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B2', 'F6')
        
        # Cyber-Cat representation
        cat_body = Triangle(color=COLOR_CAT).scale(0.15)
        cat_ear_l = Triangle(color=COLOR_CAT).scale(0.04).shift(0.08*LEFT + 0.12*UP)
        cat_ear_r = Triangle(color=COLOR_CAT).scale(0.04).shift(0.08*RIGHT + 0.12*UP)
        cat_eye_l = Dot(radius=0.015, color=COLOR_CAT).shift(0.04*LEFT + 0.04*UP)
        cat_eye_r = Dot(radius=0.015, color=COLOR_CAT).shift(0.04*RIGHT + 0.04*UP)
        cat = VGroup(cat_body, cat_ear_l, cat_ear_r, cat_eye_l, cat_eye_r)
        
        # Initial position at (1,1) in plane coordinates
        cat.move_to(plane.coords_to_point(1, 1))
        
        self.play(Create(plane), FadeIn(cat))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_MATRIX)
        
        # Matrix A = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]
        matrix_a_tex = Text(
            "A = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]", 
            color=COLOR_MATRIX,
            font_size=24
        )
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_a_tex, 'A3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Formula T(v) = Av
        formula_tex = Text(
            "T(v) = Av", 
            color=COLOR_FORMULA,
            font_size=24
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula_tex, 'A5', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Write(matrix_a_tex), Write(formula_tex))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_FORMULA)
        
        # Matrix to apply (90 degree counter-clockwise rotation)
        matrix = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]
        
        # Transform the space and the object
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            cat.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.play(Write(self.lecture[2]))
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Sequential Challenge"
        lecture_lines = [
            "We can apply two linear transformations in sequence.",
            "First, matrix A rotates our character.",
            "Then, matrix B stretches the result."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Asset Preparation ===
        # Create a "Cyber-Cat" procedural mobject
        cat_head = Circle(radius=0.25, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        cat_ear_l = Triangle(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1).rotate(30*DEGREES).shift(LEFT*0.15 + UP*0.2)
        cat_ear_r = Triangle(color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1).rotate(-30*DEGREES).shift(RIGHT*0.15 + UP*0.2)
        cat_eye_l = Dot(radius=0.03, color=BLACK).shift(LEFT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        cat_eye_r = Dot(radius=0.03, color=BLACK).shift(RIGHT*0.1 + UP*0.05)
        cat = VGroup(cat_head, cat_ear_l, cat_ear_r, cat_eye_l, cat_eye_r)
        
        # Initial state: Rotated 90 degrees CCW
        cat.rotate(90 * DEGREES)

        # Coordinate System - Using Text instead of MathTex for coordinates to avoid LaTeX dependency
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": GREY_C},
        ).add_coordinates(label_constructor=Text, font_size=20)
        
        # Place axes in the designated grid area
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Matrix B (Green) - Replaced MathTex with Text
        matrix_b = Text(
            "B = [[2, 0], [0, 1]]", 
            color="#00FF00",
            font_size=24
        )
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_b, "A2", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Composition Formula (White) - Replaced MathTex with Text
        formula = Text(
            "B(A(v))", 
            color="#FFFFFF",
            font_size=24
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Initial Position of Cat (relative to axes)
        cat.move_to(axes.c2p(-1, 1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(cat))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(cat.animate.scale(1.15), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(cat.animate.scale(1/1.15), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Write(matrix_b), Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # Execute stretching transformation (Matrix B)
        self.play(
            cat.animate.stretch(2, dim=0, about_point=axes.c2p(0,0)),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and lecture lines
        title_text = "Finding the Shortcut (The 'Why')"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Instead of two steps, we want one \"Master Matrix\".",
            "- The product matrix C performs both transformations at once.",
            "- Multiplication order is right-to-left: C = BA."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        def get_cyber_cat(color=WHITE):
            # A simple cat head with ears and eyes
            head = Circle(radius=0.3, color=color, stroke_width=2)
            ear_l = Triangle(color=color).scale(0.1).rotate(30*DEGREES).move_to(head.get_top() + LEFT*0.15 + UP*0.05)
            ear_r = Triangle(color=color).scale(0.1).rotate(-30*DEGREES).move_to(head.get_top() + RIGHT*0.15 + UP*0.05)
            eye_l = Dot(head.get_center() + LEFT*0.1 + UP*0.1, radius=0.03, color=color)
            eye_r = Dot(head.get_center() + RIGHT*0.1 + UP*0.1, radius=0.03, color=color)
            return VGroup(head, ear_l, ear_r, eye_l, eye_r)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        cat_orig = get_cyber_cat(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(cat_orig, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        label_orig = Text("Step 0", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(cat_orig, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        cat_final = get_cyber_cat(WHITE)
        cat_final.rotate(90 * DEGREES).stretch(2, dim=0)
        self.place_at_grid(cat_final, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        label_final = Text("Step 2", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(cat_final, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(cat_orig), Write(label_orig))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        arrow_shortcut = Arrow(cat_orig.get_right(), cat_final.get_left(), color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
        label_c = Text("C", color=YELLOW).next_to(arrow_shortcut, UP)

        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_shortcut), Write(label_c))
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(cat_orig, cat_final), Write(label_final))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        formula = Text("C = BA", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "D4")
        box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=BLUE, buff=SMALL_BUFF)

        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Background and Title
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side for visualization)
        self.grid_points = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Offset to the right side of the screen (x > 0)
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.0
                y = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid_points[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid_points[grid_pos])

    def construct(self):
        # 1. Initialize Layout with Topic-Specific Content
        self.setup_layout(
            "Matrix Multiplication as Composition",
            [
                "- Transformation A: Rotation",
                "- Transformation B: Scaling",
                "- Apply B then A: A(Bv)",
                "- Equivalent to (AB)v",
                "- Order of Ops: Right to Left"
            ]
        )

        # 2. Visual Elements: Coordinate System on the Right
        # Create a small plane to represent the transformation space
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )
        self.place_at_grid(plane, "C3") # Centers the plane in the grid area

        # 3. Vector and Matrices
        vector_v = Vector([1, 0], color=YELLOW)
        vector_v.shift(plane.get_origin())
        
        v_label = Text("v", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)
        v_label.next_to(vector_v, UP, buff=0.1)

        # Transformation Matrices
        # B: Scale x by 2
        # A: Rotate 90 degrees counter-clockwise
        matrix_b = [[2, 0], [0, 1]]
        matrix_a = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]

        # 4. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Create(plane), FadeIn(vector_v), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # Step 1: Apply B (Scaling)
        self.play(
            vector_v.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_b, about_point=plane.get_origin()),
            v_label.animate.next_to(plane.get_origin() + RIGHT * 2, UP),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 2: Apply A (Rotation)
        self.play(
            vector_v.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_a, about_point=plane.get_origin()),
            v_label.animate.next_to(plane.get_origin() + UP * 1, LEFT),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(RED),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Conclusion Visual
        final_formula = Text("T_total = A * B", font_size=32, color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(final_formula, "E3")
        
        self.play(Write(final_formula))
        self.play(Indicate(final_formula))
        
        self.wait(3)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section data
        title_text = "Order Matters: Non-Commutativity"
        lecture_lines = [
            "In matrix multiplication, the order of operations matters.",
            "Rotating then stretching differs from stretching then rotating.",
            "Matrix AB is usually not equal to BA.",
            "Geometry shows why multiplication is not commutative."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Matrix Definitions (Implicit in animations)
        # A: Rotation 90 degrees Counter-Clockwise
        # B: Scaling along X-axis by a factor of 2
        rot_mat = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]
        stretch_mat = [[2, 0], [0, 1]]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Setup two planes side-by-side for comparison
        plane_ba = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1], y_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1], 
            x_length=2.4, y_length=2.4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).set_color(GRAY)
        self.place_in_area(plane_ba, 'A1', 'C3')
        
        label_ba = Text("BA: Rotate then Stretch", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)
        label_ba.next_to(plane_ba, UP, buff=0.1)

        plane_ab = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1], y_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1], 
            x_length=2.4, y_length=2.4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).set_color(GRAY)
        self.place_in_area(plane_ab, 'A4', 'C6')
        
        label_ab = Text("AB: Stretch then Rotate", font_size=16, color=GREEN)
        label_ab.next_to(plane_ab, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            Create(plane_ba), Create(plane_ab),
            Write(label_ba), Write(label_ab),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Create simple representation of the "Cat" (Triangle + Eyes)
        def create_cat(color_body):
            body = Triangle(color=color_body, fill_opacity=0.8).scale(0.15)
            # Add a small dot to indicate 'front' orientation
            nose = Dot(color=BLACK).scale(0.3).move_to(body.get_top())
            return VGroup(body, nose)

        cat_ba = create_cat(WHITE)
        cat_ba.move_to(plane_ba.c2p(1, 0)) # Start at point (1, 0)
        
        cat_ab = create_cat(WHITE)
        cat_ab.move_to(plane_ab.c2p(1, 0)) # Start at point (1, 0)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with section title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Real-World Connection", [
            "Matrix multiplication glues multiple geometric steps together.",
            "It \"bakes\" complex movements into a single matrix.",
            "This is essential for CGI and robotics."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight current lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Create sequence of matrices M3 * M2 * M1 = M
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' command dependency
        m1 = Text("M1", color="#88C0D0", slant=ITALIC) # Light Blue
        m2 = Text("M2", color="#A3BE8C", slant=ITALIC) # Light Green
        m3 = Text("M3", color="#EBCB8B", slant=ITALIC) # Light Yellow
        dot1 = Text("·", color=WHITE)
        dot2 = Text("·", color=WHITE)
        eq = Text("=", color=WHITE)
        m_final = Text("M", color="#B48EAD", slant=ITALIC) # Light Purple
        
        matrix_sequence = VGroup(m3, dot1, m2, dot2, m1, eq, m_final).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_sequence, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        # Animate writing the sequence
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                Write(m3), Write(dot1), Write(m2), Write(dot2), Write(m1),
                lag_ratio=0.3
            )
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Show condensation into M
        product_vgroup = VGroup(m3, dot1, m2, dot2, m1)
        self.play(
            Write(eq),
            Transform(product_vgroup.copy(), m_final, remover=True),
            Write(m_final)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Switch highlight to the second line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Create a simple line-diagram robotic arm in #C0C0C0
        arm_color = "#C0C0C0"
        base_point = self.grid["D2"].copy() 
        
        # Pre-build arm components
        shoulder = Dot(base_point, color=arm_color)
        upper_arm = Line(base_point, base_point + RIGHT * 1.5, color=arm_color)
        
        elbow_point = upper_arm.get_end()
        elbow = Dot(elbow_point, color=arm_color)
        forearm = Line(elbow_point, elbow_point + RIGHT * 1.0, color=arm_color)
        
        wrist_point = forearm.get_end()
        wrist = Dot(wrist_point, color=arm_color)
        hand = Line(wrist_point, wrist_point + RIGHT * 0.5, color=arm_color)
        
        arm_elements = VGroup(shoulder, upper_arm, elbow, forearm, wrist, hand)
        
        self.play(Create(arm_elements))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # ValueTrackers for joint angles to simulate "baking" movements
        theta1 = ValueTracker(0)
        theta2 = ValueTracker(0)
        theta3 = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Efficient updater using pre-calculated points
        def update_arm(mob):
            t1 = theta1.get_value() * DEGREES
            t2 = theta2.get_value() * DEGREES
            t3 = theta3.get_value() * DEGREES
            
            p0 = base_point
            p1 = p0 + np.array([np.cos(t1), np.sin(t1), 0]) * 1.5
            p2 = p1 + np.array([np.cos(t1 + t2), np.sin(t1 + t2), 0]) * 1.0
            p3 = p2 + np.array([np.cos(t1 + t2 + t3), np.sin(t1 + t2 + t3), 0]) * 0.5
            
            upper_arm.put_start_and_end_on(p0, p1)
            elbow.move_to(p1)
            forearm.put_start_and_end_on(p1, p2)
            wrist.move_to(p2)
            hand.put_start_and_end_on(p2, p3)

        arm_elements.add_updater(update_arm)
        
        # Animate the arm moving smoothly (simulating baked transformation)
        self.play(
            theta1.animate.set_value(-20),
            theta2.animate.set_value(45),
            theta3.animate.set_value(30),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Switch highlight to the third line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Complex movement showing multi-joint coordination (essential for robotics/CGI)
        self.play(
            theta1.animate.set_value(40),
            theta2.animate.set_value(-70),
            theta3.animate.set_value(-40),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=bezier([0, 0, 1, 1])
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Cleanup
        arm_elements.remove_updater(update_arm)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Matrix as a Machine
sections.content: Briefly review that a 2x2 matrix acts as a function (linear transformation) that moves points in 2D space. Visualize a 2D grid with a character (e.g., a 'Cyber-Cat') sitting on it. Applying matrix A transforms the cat (e.g., rotates it). Introduce the notation T(v) = Av.
sections.example: A 'Cyber-Cat' at coordinates (1,1) is rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise by matrix A = [[0, -1], [1, 0]].

sections.title: The Sequential Challenge
sections.content: Introduce the concept of applying two transformations in a row. First, apply transformation A (rotation), then apply transformation B (scaling/stretching). Show the Cyber-Cat rotating first, and then the rotated cat getting stretched. This defines the composition B(A(v)).
sections.example: The rotated Cyber-Cat is now stretched horizontally by matrix B = [[2, 0], [0, 1]]. We see the cat move twice.

sections.title: Finding the Shortcut (The 'Why')
sections.content: Explain the motivation: instead of calculating two separate steps for every point, we want a single 'Master Matrix' C that performs both actions in one leap. This Master Matrix C is the product of B and A (C = BA). Emphasize the right-to-left order of operations.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Teleportation Gate' where the original cat enters and the rotated-then-stretched cat instantly exits on the other side.

sections.title: The Mechanics: Basis Vector Tracking
sections.content: Graphically demonstrate why we multiply 'Rows by Columns'. Follow the basis vectors i-hat (1,0) and j-hat (0,1). Show that the columns of matrix BA represent where the basis vectors end up after undergoing transformation A then transformation B.
sections.example: Animate the i-hat vector: first it rotates to (0,1) via A, then it is scaled to (0,1) via B. This tracking forms the first column of the resulting product matrix.

sections.title: Order Matters: Non-Commutativity
sections.content: Use the visual nature of transformations to show why AB is not the same as BA. Changing the order of transformations usually results in a different final position for our character.
sections.example: Compare two scenarios: (1) Rotate then Stretch vs. (2) Stretch then Rotate. Show the Cyber-Cat ending up in two completely different orientations on the grid.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Connection
sections.content: Recap that matrix multiplication is just the mathematical 'glue' that binds multiple geometric steps together. Briefly mention applications in computer graphics (CGI) or robotics where hundreds of transformations are 'baked' into one matrix.
sections.example: A 3D character in a video game moving its arm: the movement is a composition of rotation matrices at the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints.

Matrix AB is usually not equal to BA.
